introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2024. Time allowed: three hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklet are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (One hour): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (30 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (1 hour): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.

3(c)(i) : la résistance thermique est prise comme R = x/(kA) (en K/W), définition usuelle ; 3(c)(ii) : débit de chaleur = (T1 - T2)/R, soit P = kA(T1 - T2)/x.

questions.enonce_markdown: State two conditions for the heat conduction through the wall above to reach a steady state.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Any two of the following (each stated clearly):

1. The temperature at every point of the wall has become constant, i.e. the two faces are maintained at constant temperatures $T_1$ and $T_2$ ($T_1 > T_2$), so that the wall no longer absorbs heat to raise its own temperature.
2. The rate at which heat enters the inner face equals the rate at which it leaves the outer face ($Q_1 = Q_2$ in the same time): no heat is lost through the sides of the wall (the edges are lagged), so the heat flows only perpendicular to the faces.
3. The wall is uniform (same material and constant cross-section), so the temperature falls uniformly (linearly) through the wall: the temperature gradient is constant.

questions.enonce_markdown: Define temperature gradient and write an expression for it for the wall.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Definition.** The temperature gradient is the rate of change of temperature with distance in the direction of heat flow, i.e. the temperature difference per unit length along the direction of heat flow. Its unit is $\mathrm{K\,m^{-1}}$.

**Expression for the wall.** In the steady state the temperature falls uniformly from $T_1$ to $T_2$ over the thickness $x$, so
$$\text{temperature gradient} = \frac{\Delta T}{\Delta x} = \frac{T_1 - T_2}{x}\quad\left(\text{or } \frac{\mathrm{d}T}{\mathrm{d}x} = -\frac{T_1 - T_2}{x},\ \text{negative because } T \text{ decreases along the flow}\right).$$

**(i) Thermal resistance.** With $x = 12.0\ \mathrm{cm} = 0.120\ \mathrm{m}$,
$$R = \frac{x}{kA} = \frac{0.120}{0.80\times0.08} = 1.875\ \mathrm{K\,W^{-1}}\approx1.9\ \mathrm{K\,W^{-1}}.$$

**(ii) Rate of heat flow.** The temperature difference is $T_1 - T_2 = 355 - 330 = 25\ \mathrm{K}$, so
$$\frac{Q}{t} = \frac{T_1 - T_2}{R} = \frac{25}{1.875} = 13.3\ \mathrm{W}.$$
(Check with $\dfrac{Q}{t} = \dfrac{kA(T_1 - T_2)}{x} = \dfrac{0.80\times0.08\times25}{0.120} = 13.3\ \mathrm{W}$.)

**Rate of heat flow $\approx 13\ \mathrm{W}$.**
